Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

breedtools 0.1.0

  • First CRAN release.
  • Documentation website (pkgdown) with every function grouped by task, and a grouped list of all functions with examples in the README.
  • Names saved in Breedbase contain only letters, digits, “”, ”-” and ”.”: in trial, plot, new folder and analysis names, spaces and characters such as % $ ( ) { } [ ]  / < > * become ”” (e.g. location “Alcobaca (BA)” gives trial “EMBRAPA_2026_Alcobaca_BA”). Accession and location names are kept, existing folders are used as they are, and trials can still be looked up by the original name.
  • save_breedbase_analysis() has folder and create_folder: the analysis is put in a folder of the program (as the website’s “Move to folder”), instead of directly in the breeding program.
  • New breedbase_check() checks the location(s) and every entry and check (as accessions) in Breedbase before a design is built, plus the program, folder and trial name when given. All problems are listed together with close matches (e.g. “ibadan” -> “Ibadan”). save_breedbase() now reports location and accession problems together too.
  • Breedbase searches work on slow servers: accessions are searched 25 at a time and a batch that times out (HTTP 504/502/503/429) is split and tried again, with a line after each batch (names done, percent, time). Accessions found are remembered for the R session, so save_breedbase() after breedbase_check() does not search them again.
  • save_breedbase() survives server timeouts when writing: after a timeout it checks whether the folder, trial or plots were created before trying again (no duplicates), and a re-run continues a save that was cut off (an existing folder is used; a trial without plots gets its plots).
  • breedbase_check() says plainly when the trial already exists (“choose another trial_name”), and that an existing folder is fine: the trial is saved inside it. save_breedbase() also uses a folder that Breedbase reports as existing when it tries to create it.
  • The folder of save_breedbase() is optional: without it the trial is saved directly in the breeding program.
  • save_breedbase() sends the germplasmDbId of each accession with the plots, which Breedbase requires (“Verify Germplasm Id.” error before).
  • New save_breedbase_phenotypes() saves phenotypic data to Breedbase by plot name and trait name (wide: one column per trait, or long: trait and value columns; optional time stamps for repeated measurements). Plots and traits are checked first, values are sent in batches (surviving server timeouts) and read back to verify. New phenotype_template() makes the phenotyping sheet with the Breedbase plot names of a design.
  • Analysis results to Breedbase. First stage: first_stage_values() gives one value per field plot (adjusted mean of the genotype + plot residual, design and spatial effects removed) and save_breedbase_first_stage() saves it on the field plots as its own trait: the measured trait composed with a statistic (“fresh root yield|Adjusted Means from Spatial Correction using SpATS R”), found or created by breedbase_adjusted_trait(). Second stage: second_stage_values() collects the genotype adjusted means and save_breedbase_analysis() saves them as a Breedbase analysis, like the Breedbase mixed-models tool.
  • analyze_resolvable_row_column() now returns plot_results with the fitted values and plot residuals.
  • New analyze_two_stage(): two-stage analysis of a multi-location trial for every design (augmented row-column, augmented p-rep, resolvable row-column), with a SpATS spatial stage 1 (default) or the design’s own model, and the weighted stage 2 of analyze_augmented_prep_two_stage().
  • New compare_first_stage(): raw against first-stage adjusted plot values per location (correlation, spread, change in genotype ranking), with raw and adjusted field maps.
  • New find_outliers() and remove_outliers(): IQR rule (multiplier 1.5 by default) within each location; removed values are set to NA and listed by plot.
  • New plot_trait(): histogram and field map of a trait per location, with outliers circled.
  • analyze_augmented_row_column_design() returns adjusted_means_vcov; with spatial = TRUE or random effects, plot_results residuals now come from that model (they came from the fixed model before).
  • breedbase_login() has site_username / site_password for test sites with an extra web password in front of the website (BrAPI works without it, the trait composer and analyses need it); a clear message says so. Usually not needed: at login, when a site’s web pages ask for a password, the Breedbase login is tried there and used if it works.
  • breedbase_adjusted_trait() finds an existing adjusted trait through BrAPI first, so the first stage needs no web page when the trait exists.
  • Breedbase’s BrAPI upload does not refresh the phenotype cache that its trial pages and search wizard read, so saved values did not show there. save_breedbase_phenotypes() and save_breedbase_first_stage() now ask Breedbase to refresh it; new breedbase_refresh() does it on demand.
  • No fixed Breedbase terms: the statistic of first- and second-stage results is chosen from the server’s own statistic terms (new breedbase_statistics() lists them), a given statistic is checked against the server, and composed traits are matched by their components. A model type unknown to the server gives a clear message.
  • save_breedbase_analysis() uses the same upload as Breedbase’s “Upload analysis” form (name, description, protocol, breeding program, statistic, optional time terms) with Breedbase’s model type for uploaded results, and has level = "plot" (“Analysis of: plots”): first-stage values become an analysis with one plot per field plot, linked by Breedbase to the field trial.
  • Statistics are checked against the Breedbase statistics ontology (cxgn_statistics.obo from the Breedbase source, included in the package): a statistic must be a real SGNSTAT term, a given id must belong to the given name, and misspelled names get suggestions; breedbase_statistics() lists the terms without a server.
  • Sites whose web pages need their own web password (e.g. cassava-test): the login asks for it; without it, save_breedbase_analysis() checks everything through BrAPI and writes the file of the website’s “Upload analysis” form, printing every form field to fill in.
  • New breedbase_phenotypes() reads the phenotypes of a list of trials and traits from Breedbase (plots with accession, rep, block, row, column).
  • New analyze_single_stage(): all trials in one model (lme4, or SpATS with spatial = TRUE: trials side by side, each with its own spatial trend), to compare with the two-stage analysis.
  • analyze_two_stage(stage1 = "blocks"): a first stage without a design object, for data read from Breedbase; first_stage_values() works without a design for such data.
  • add_breedbase_analysis_values(statistic = ) stores values under “trait|statistic”, so several analyses (e.g. two-stage and single-stage means) can sit in the same analysis project.
  • New add_breedbase_analysis_values() adds results (e.g. a second trait) to an analysis already in Breedbase, through the phenotype upload of the website: Breedbase verifies the file first, and values already stored are not replaced unless overwrite = TRUE.
  • The script has three Breedbase switches (save_designs, save_phenotypes, save_analyses), a trial-name prefix and a run tag for unique analysis names, and saves analyses only for trials in Breedbase.
  • New breedbase_trial_plots() reads the plots of a saved trial; first_stage_values(breedbase_plots = ) checks that the design in R is the one saved (same accession at every plot number) and uses the saved plot names.
  • scripts/validate_designs.R is organized in one part per design, each from the field plan to the results in Breedbase. See options(breedtools.germplasm_batch) and options(breedtools.breedbase_timeout).
  • New save_breedbase() saves any design (augmented row-column, p-rep, resolvable row-column) as a trial with its plots in a ‘Breedbase’ database through BrAPI v2, in a chosen breeding program and folder. It checks the program, folder (optionally created), locations, accessions and trial name before writing, asks for confirmation, and reads the plots back to verify. dry_run = TRUE makes all checks without writing. Plot names are made automatically as trialName_accession_block_rep (plot_name_pattern) or given by you (plot_names), and are checked to be new in the database. breedbase_login() logs in without storing the password; breedbase_programs(), breedbase_folders() and breedbase_locations() list what exists.
  • New resolvable row-column designs (Williams, John and Whitaker, 2006):
    • resolvable_row_column_design() builds designs for v <= k * s treatments in r replicates of k x s, optimizing the row-column, row and column efficiency factors and then the spatial (LV + RC) efficiency factor. Latinized and t-latinized designs for contiguous replicates, filler plots, and improving or laying out an existing design (start_design) are supported.
    • resolvable_row_column_efficiency() reports the efficiency factors, the spatial upper bound, the AR-model criterion z(X), and treatment neighbour and edge counts.
    • analyze_resolvable_row_column() fits the RC, LV + RC and AR + RC models by REML and compares them by deviance; long columns of latinized designs can be fitted as fixed.
    • plot_resolvable_row_column_design() draws the field.
  • augmented_row_column_design():
    • Check placement now uses covering Latin rectangles, so every field row and column gets a check.
    • Layouts whose effects cannot be estimated, or that leave no error degrees of freedom, are rejected.
    • The design is much faster to generate.
  • New helpers for checking designs and simulations: check_setup() checks at the start of a script that breedtools, the optional ‘lme4’ and ‘SpATS’ packages and the output folder are ready, check_design() runs the standard checks of any design and prints [OK] / [FAIL] lines, check_result() records a check of your own, check_section() groups the following checks, check_summary() reports what was checked by section and what is correct, check_reset() clears the tally (saying how many checks it cleared), and prediction_accuracy() gives the correlation between adjusted means and known true values.
  • New augmented_row_column_layouts() lists every analyzable layout of a field (block sizes and numbers of checks), most entry plots first, with optional n_entries and min_error_df filters.
  • augmented_row_column_capacity() reports the error degrees of freedom of a layout, the share of check plots, and the row-group and column-group conditions of Piepho and Williams (2016).
  • Augmented row-column designs now support the full strategy of Piepho and Williams (2016): row and column groups of unequal size (rows_per_rowgroup, cols_per_colgroup) and any number of check plots per block (checks_per_block), giving incomplete blocks or extra check replication. The new method = "optimal" allocates checks by a D-optimal local search that keeps check plots from being neighbours (same column in consecutive rows, or same row in consecutive columns) and keeps the check allocation balanced: a block with at least as many check plots as checks holds every check (extra plots repeat checks), an incomplete block holds each check at most once, rows and columns of a group get even numbers of check plots, and a column (or row) with room for all checks holds every check. Figures 3 and 4 of Piepho and Williams (2016) are reproduced with all their stated properties; "latin" keeps the covering Latin rectangle construction (now with evenly spaced check rows and columns, and polished by swapping rows or columns within groups to remove neighbouring checks), and "auto" picks it when it applies. summary reports the D-criterion.
  • analyze_augmented_row_column_design() can take rows, columns and blocks as random to recover inter-block information (random_blocks = TRUE), model entries as random with fixed checks (entries = "random", BLUPs), or add a spatial P-spline surface with ‘SpATS’ (spatial = TRUE).
  • analyze_augmented_row_column_design():
    • Degrees of freedom are corrected (rows within row groups k - gk, columns within column groups s - gs), and the ANOVA uses the df that are estimable from the observed plots.
    • The model is fitted by absorbing unreplicated entries, so it is fast for large fields.
  • augmented_prep_design() uses a faster candidate search with incremental concurrence scoring. The search stops early once an optimal design is found.
  • augmented_prep_design() follows Williams, Piepho and Whitaker (2011) more closely:
    • p-rep plots are spread evenly over the blocks of each location;
    • the blocks of each location are kept connected by the p-rep entries, so each location can be analysed on its own (a warning is given when there are too few p-rep plots to do so);
    • a swap-based improvement step removes pairs of entries that share more than one block, giving (0,1)-designs for cases such as the paper’s six-location trial with blocks of eight; repeated concurrences are penalized quadratically, so when a (0,1)-design is out of reach the excess is spread over pairs instead of one pair meeting at every location, and greedy candidates that put an entry twice in a block are repaired instead of discarded;
    • new resolvable = TRUE option builds a resolvable design at each location (every p-rep entry once per replicate), returned in the new replicate column;
    • summary reports the average efficiency factor (efficiency_factor) and the number of disconnected locations; among optimal candidates the most efficient one is returned (n_efficiency_candidates).
    • new method argument chooses the construction: "search" (default), "alpha" (partial alpha-arrays, Sections 2.1-2.2 of the paper) or "alpha2" (augmented alpha(2)-arrays, Section 2.4), with n_prep_per_block for the number of p-rep entries per block (m).
  • New analyze_augmented_prep_two_stage(): two-stage analysis of multi-location p-rep trials. Stage 1 analyses each location with its own error variance, either with the incomplete-block model or with a spatial P-spline model from the suggested ‘SpATS’ package (stage1 = "spatial"). Stage 2 combines the location means with full or diagonal stage-1 weighting (Möhring and Piepho, 2009) and a REML genotype-by-location variance. It reports Hartley’s Fmax test of heterogeneous error variances.
  • analyze_augmented_prep_design() returns the covariance matrix of the adjusted means ($adjusted_means_vcov).
  • Methods "alpha" and "alpha2" stop searching once further random starts no longer help, and warn when no (0,1)-design was found.
  • New augmented_prep_parameters() lists the feasible parameter sets of the algebraic constructions (as in Table 3 of the paper).
  • map_environment_groups() now uses the same maps as the ‘Breedbase’ Locations page by default (tiles = "breedbase"): Esri Street, Topographical and Satellite, with a switch between them. They need no account or API key and work in the RStudio viewer. tiles can also be "street", "topo", "satellite", "OpenStreetMap" or a leaflet provider name.
  • plot_augmented_prep_design() draws clearer maps: entries repeated at the location in orange with bold names (they replace the checks), single plots in light grey, thick black lines around blocks, a blue line and labels for replicates, a plain-language legend, a caption explaining the map (caption = TRUE), and locations in the order of the design. It can also colour plots by replicate.
  • analyze_augmented_prep_design():
    • Handles single-location trials.
    • Reports df that are estimable when plots are missing.
  • analyze_augmented_prep_design() fits replicates within locations for resolvable designs (replicate_col) and can add a genotype-by-location interaction, fixed (genotype_by_location = "fixed") or random ("random", REML via the suggested ‘lme4’ package, with variance components in $variance_components).
  • Both analyses now return adjusted entry means (BLUEs) with standard errors ($adjusted_means), and report the mean SED and the 5% LSD in $diagnostics.
  • New tutorial, vignette("breedtools"), covering every design and analysis and the multi-environment tools, and an RStudio workflow script in inst/examples. The source package includes scripts/validate_designs.R, a step-by-step tour of every design and analysis with simple checks, and scripts/run_all_checks.R, the full automated validation against the published examples, lm(), ‘lme4’ and simulation.
